recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-25089 unless a future work-group issue intentionally revises license-page messaging.
issue_request: FHIR-25089 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR Infrastructure change request for the FHIR-core license page. It asked HL7 to add a Promoting interoperability paragraph below Disclaimer and Warning of Use so the page better communicates the open spirit of FHIR's CC0 license.
initial_application: PR HL7/fhir#2417 applied the issue. Commit d4a14dd4e859f769c94ba9154b2be7255bc3c6f4 added the Promoting Interoperability heading and CC0/public-domain adoption paragraph to source/license.html for FHIR-25089, and merge commit 03e2bf012913416912370b4eae031dd7ce9a680f brought the PR into the source history. A same-day follow-up, 6521f07bd26637710cf04cc8753d5e5e7c0d7e7b, repositioned the R5 ballot/TODO warning while preserving the new section.
additional_context: The 2022-09-13 Zulip social thread reviewed the proposed wording as an additional paragraph, and the 2022-09 FHIR-I WGM Confluence minutes record FHIR-25089 as persuasive with a 14-0-0 vote and the approved healthcare-to-health-care wording adjustment. source/hierarchy.xml lists license.html as the License and Legal Terms page, confirming the inspected source page is in current specification navigation scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/license.html:27-35 already contains the Promoting Interoperability section immediately after the disclaimer, including the CC0 1.0/public-domain rationale, patient empowerment, and interoperable-health-data availability language.
